caveats: A single sampled launch per variant is stochastic.
Observed stall differences do not decompose elapsed time.
The static causal register allocation changes from 127 to 125; its pre-epilogue code is not encoding-identical.
The other three kernels have encoding-identical prefixes before the epilogue.
The reference has an LTC128B copy modifier; the retained cuda-oxide kernels have the plain copy form. A separate controlled cache-hint probe established no consistent meaningful benefit.
These counters identify the eliminated address work and remaining differences; they do not establish that all remaining timing is explained.
conclusions: The final kernels execute fewer dynamic warp instructions than both the preceding combined address/copy build and the matched reference in all four modes.

Static noncausal and both runtime modes save 16,384 dynamic instructions entirely in the epilogue, with no instruction-count change outside it. Static causal saves 16,896 in the epilogue but adds 3,360 elsewhere, for a net saving of 13,536.

The static-causal allocation change replaces one hoisted pointer addition with a uniform constant load and a repeated loop addition. Its added 2,880 IADD.64 and 480 LDCU.64 executions exactly account for the 3,360 instructions outside the epilogue.
Copy instruction counts, shared wavefronts and global theoretical sectors match the previous build and reference. Matrix instruction counts and epilogue memory-operation counts also match.

HMMA short-scoreboard observations are zero in both static modes, one in runtime causal and 226 in runtime noncausal. Runtime noncausal remains concentrated at the unchanged 0x2230 consumer, with 191 observations. The small changes from the previous sampled launch do not establish a regression; runtime pre-epilogue encodings are identical.
The epilogue cleanup removes specific address work. These counters and sampled stalls do not assign an exact fraction of elapsed time to that work or explain every remaining reference gap.

static_causal_address_tradeoff.interpretation: One hoisted pointer addition is replaced by a uniform constant load and a repeated loop addition, consistent with the changed register allocation. This is a precise instruction-count tradeoff, not a latency decomposition.
